newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Iceland says grounded ship unlikely to be saved.
newsitem.headline: Iceland says grounded ship unlikely to be saved.

text.p: A salvage crew will next week remove all cargo and oil from a German container ship which ran aground off Iceland three days ago but it was unlikely the ship can be saved, the Icelandic coast guard said on Saturday.

The 8,000- tonne Vikartindur ran aground on Wednesday about 1.5 nautical miles from the Icelandic coast after being struck by a heavy wave. It had been drifting for about two hours because of engine trouble.
A coast guard official said the ship was buried in sand and had a big crack in the middle.
"It is very unlikely they will be able to save the ship," the official told Reuters by telephone from Reykjavik.
"A salvage crew will on Monday try to take all the cargo and remaining oil from the ship before they look at any salvage attempt."
One Icelandic coast guard worker fell overboard in an attempt to tow the vessel after it went aground on Wednesday. The body had not been recovered.
All 19 of the German crew were safe after being rescued from the ship by helicopter.
The ship was leased by Iceland's largest shipping company, Eimskip, and owned by German shipping company Peter Dohle Schiffahrts Kg.
The ship was carrying 4,000 containers of mixed cargo from Germany to Iceland, the official said.
